study type: Cross-sectional epidemiological study, nested in a cohort
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (2020) vs. pre-pandemic period (2011-2012)
outcome: Breastfeeding within the first hour after delivery
cohort: The study included 1082 women who gave birth during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and 382 women who gave birth in 2011-2012, all from Brazil.
finding: The study found that women in the pre-pandemic period had a higher proportion of early breastfeeding, fewer indications for cesarean section, and fewer obstetric complications compared to the pandemic period; furthermore, during the pandemic, cesarean section, low birth weight, and newborn complications significantly reduced the chance of breastfeeding after delivery.
mod_finding: Women who underwent cesarean section reduced their chance of breastfeeding after delivery, especially during the pandemic period, and a higher proportion of early breastfeeding was observed in the pre-pandemic period among women without an indication for cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collected in 2020 (pandemic period) and 2011-2012 (pre-pandemic period)
birth_weight: Newborns weighing less than 2500g were identified as a factor reducing the chance of breastfeeding.
